div.div: Every decision, signal, compromise and policy change is appended to a JSONL log where each entry commits to the one before it. Editing or deleting any entry breaks every later link (IEC 62443 SR 2.8, NIST tenet 7).

ul.li: ztcctl audit verify: recompute every hash from genesis
restart: OpenFile reads the JSONL and continues from the last hash so a restart never breaks the chain
HLC timestamps (M3): logs from several nodes merge in causal order
export: syslog to a SIEM, where a copy lives outside the attacker's reach

hash so a restart never breaks the chainHLC timestamps (M3): logs from several nodes merge in causal orderexport:
syslog to a SIEM, where a copy lives outside the attacker's reach

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 786px; height: 1px; padding-top: 540px; margin-left: 28px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 15px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

ul.li: an attacker with write access to the whole file can rebuild the entire chain
mitigation: anchor the head hash elsewhere (SIEM, Raft log, signed checkpoints)
the log is evidence, not prevention: detection and accountability (STRIDE R)

div.b: Why a hash chain and not a database?

ul.li: append-only by construction, verifiable with 30 lines of Go
no extra service in the trust path
same idea as certificate transparency and git, without a Merkle tree (not needed at this size)
